queries: ARC Prize o3 ARC-AGI-Pub results December 2024

sources_considered.why: The benchmark operator's own analysis of o3 on a novel-task benchmark, with human comparisons.
A large perturbation study of frontier LLMs on math reasoning, published October 2024.

receipt.public_excerpt: I don't think o3 is AGI yet. o3 still fails on some very easy tasks, indicating fundamental differences with human intelligence.

evidence_items.explanation: The benchmark's creator says that even the strongest system of the time still failed very easy novel tasks and was not human-level general intelligence.

receipt.public_excerpt: potentially reducing its score to under 30% even at high compute (while a smart human would still be able to score over 95% with no training).

evidence_items.explanation: Early tests showed a large gap between the best model and humans on fresh novel tasks. That fits a lack of reliable generalization.

receipt.public_excerpt: Specifically, the performance of all models declines when only the numerical values in the question are altered in the GSM-Symbolic benchmark.

evidence_items.explanation: Every model tested got worse when only the numbers in familiar problems changed. That shows unreliable generalization to slightly new cases. The page read is v2; v1 was posted 2024-10-07.

evidence_items.locator: section 'OpenAI o3 ARC-AGI Results', paragraph after results table

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI's new o3 model represents a significant leap forward in AI's ability to adapt to novel tasks.

evidence_items.explanation: o3 showed a real jump in adapting to novel tasks (75.7% on ARC-AGI-1). That partly cuts against a flat 'lack the ability to generalize', though not against 'reliably' or human-level.

unresolved_gaps: Exact released-model results on ARC-AGI-2 came after the target period, so they were not used.
The o3 result tested a preview system trained on ARC public training data.
